title: Chandra separates the two X-ray nuclei of ESO 253-G003: the steady hard X-rays are an obscured companion AGN, and ASASSN-14ko has an on-off soft state with late UV peaks in off cycles
abstract: Question: the X-ray clock of the repeating nuclear transient ASASSN-14ko (a sharp soft X-ray drop 5.5 d before each UV peak, constant 108.44-d period in 2020-2024) and the test that its AGN stayed steady when the period decrease stopped both use data that blend the two AGN of ESO 253-G003. Which nucleus makes the dip, and why do the 2022 flares have no X-ray ingress? Approach: we reduced all 13 public Chandra ACIS-S visits (2020-2023, including nine of cycle 26 in 2022 and two inside the cycle-30 dip), registered them on field sources, and fitted two point sources jointly. We added 14 NuSTAR visits and the XMM-Newton pn spectra of the cycle-30 dip. Results: the two nuclei are 1.6 arcsec apart and match the two Gaia DR3 sources. The south-western companion is steady (2-7 keV scatter 9 percent, chi2 = 6.8 for 7 dof), obscured (N_H about 9e23 cm^-2, intrinsic L(2-10 keV) about 1.9e43 erg/s) and gives 81-95 percent of the hard counts in low states. NuSTAR 10-30 keV does not change at the dip (ratio 1.03 +/- 0.03). The component that switches off is soft and unabsorbed (kT 0.09 keV plus a power law); partial covering is excluded and full covering needs N_H >= 2e24. ASASSN-14ko itself was X-ray faint before flare 26 (hard rate 19 times lower than in January 2021), so 2022 had no state to switch off, and it burst 1.1 d after the predicted UV peak. The pre-flare soft state was on in cycles 19-25, 30, 31, 33 and off in 26, 28, 29. In off cycles the UVW2 peaks are +4.9 d late against the X-ray clock, compared with +0.2 d in on cycles (2.6 sigma with 1.2 d jitter). Conclusion: the X-ray clock marks the end of a soft state of the ASASSN-14ko nucleus; the period did not react to a change of its X-ray output by a factor of 7-19; part of the UV/optical period noise is a state-dependent emission delay. The quiescent Swift hard-band AGN check of earlier work measured the companion, and the companion can give about 0.3 of the blended WISE W2 flux, which weakens but does not remove the disc-state exclusion. Limitations: only three off cycles, consecutive in 2022; no CIAO/SAS processing; phenomenological spectral model.

display.caption: Chandra images of the galaxy centre (registered frame, west to the right). Left: eight low-state visits; right: two 2022 burst visits; top 0.5-2 keV, bottom 2-7 keV. In the low state the hard X-rays come from the south-western companion S; in the bursts the ASASSN-14ko nucleus N dominates.

Cycle 30: XMM-Newton pn and NuSTAR rates relative to the pre-dip level (the dip is absent at 10-30 keV), and pn spectra before and in the dip with the switching soft component and the steady absorbed component.
UVW2 peak minus the X-ray clock by pre-flare soft X-ray state (top) and the pre-flare level per cycle (bottom). Off cycles 28 and 29 have the latest UV peaks.

citations.reason: We use its Swift XRT counts, XMM band rates and linear X-ray clock. Chandra shows that its ingress is the switch-off of the ASASSN-14ko nucleus and that the dip floor is the companion AGN; the clock itself is supported.
We use its pre-dip levels per cycle. Chandra confirms that cycle 26, like its cycles 28-29, had no pre-flare soft state, so the missing 2022 markers are physical, not a sampling gap.

Its quiescent Swift 2-10 keV AGN check measured mostly the obscured companion nucleus, and its WISE W2 flux blends both AGN; the disc-state exclusion becomes weaker (N ratio up to 1.27 at 95 percent for a 0.6 companion share).
We use its Swift UVOT UVW2 photometry for cycle 26.
Part of the period noise that it fitted as orbital kicks coincides with the 2022 X-ray off state, where UV peaks are 4-5 d late against the X-ray clock.
Its period noise beyond a cubic trend partly comes from the late UV peaks of the 2022 X-ray off cycles.
We find an observable predictor of a changing emission delay of about 4-5 d: the pre-flare soft X-ray state.
The 2022 flares with changed shapes coincide with the X-ray off state of the ASASSN-14ko nucleus.
Late flares and the period stall of ASASSN-14ko.
SPHEREx timing of the 2025-2026 flares; context for the flare-41 forecast.
Payne et al. resolved the two nuclei in 2020-2021 Chandra data and assigned the hard X-rays to the southern nucleus; we extend this to 2022-2023 and to the dip.
Tucker et al. found the second AGN in ESO 253-G003 with MUSE.
